newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ex-soldiers jailed for "racist" assault.
newsitem.headline: German ex-soldiers jailed for "racist" assault.

text.p: Five former German soldiers were found guilty on Thursday of clubbing two Turks with baseball bats and threatening an Italian with a knife while shouting racist abuse.
The court in the western town of Detmold heard that the five aged 20 or 21 went on the rampage in March wearing army uniforms and shouting at the three foreigners: "We're coming to get you."

The dfendants, who have since been dismissed by the army, had been drinking heavily and said they had wanted revenge for an attack a week earlier by 15 young foreigners who had called them "Nazis" and "Army pigs".
They were convicted of causing serious injury. They admitted attacking the foreigners but denied shouting extreme right-wing slogans. Police later confiscated neo-Nazi propaganda from two of them.

Prosecutors said one of the defendants, Mirco Anders, 21, who held a knife to the Italian's throat according to fellow assailants, had "dangerous tendencies." He was jailed for one year and two months.
Two others were given suspended sentences of eight months and the other two received six-month suspended sentences.
Presiding judge Michael Reineke said they had carried out a racist attack, adding: "This deed can not be compared to a bar brawl. Here people were attacked by assailants in helmets and uniforms."

Their victims were treated in hospital for head injuries after the attack, which prompted Defence Minister Volker Ruehe to order a special inquiry and hundreds of people in Detmold to take to the streets in an anti-racist demonstration.
Separate proceedings will be brought against four other former soldiers who are suspected of taking part in the attack but not of inflicting bodily harm.
The army said the suspects had all just joined the army and most of them were from formerly communist east Germany.
